tasks.currentSketch: Induct on the leading monomial of a symmetric polynomial f. Its lexicographically largest term has exponents λ₁≥…≥λₙ; subtract a suitable multiple of e₁^(λ₁−λ₂)e₂^(λ₂−λ₃)…eₙ^λₙ to cancel it. The leading monomial decreases; iteration expresses f in elementary symmetric polynomials.

tasks.currentSketch: The invariant ring under Sₙ acting by permuting variables is k[x₁,…,xₙ]^{Sₙ}=k[e₁,…,eₙ]. The fundamental theorem follows by proving these generators are algebraically independent and that every invariant reduces to a polynomial in them via leading-term elimination. This is the invariant-theoretic restatement of route 1, not a wholly distinct proof.

tasks.currentSketch: Use (tI−A)adj(tI−A)=det(tI−A)I as a polynomial matrix identity. Write adjugate as ΣBᵢtⁱ and compare coefficients; a telescoping recurrence among Bᵢ, multiplied by powers of A and summed, cancels all terms and leaves χ_A(A)=0. Do not naively substitute A=t into a matrix identity with noncommuting coefficients.

tasks.routeTitle: polynomial interpolation on eigenvalues (with hypotheses carefully controlled)
tasks.currentSketch: Triangularize A over an algebraic closure. Every diagonal entry λ is an eigenvalue, so χ_A(t)=∏(t−λᵢ); the triangular matrix χ_A(A) has zero diagonal and is nilpotent, not automatically zero. Therefore this argument alone is insufficient; strengthen with generalized eigenspaces, where (A−λI)^{m_λ}=0 and χ_A contains that factor, to obtain zero on each primary component.

tasks.routeTitle: Extend a basis of the kernel
tasks.currentSketch: Choose a basis u₁,…,uₖ of ker T and extend it to a basis u₁,…,uₖ,v₁,…,vᵣ of V. Then Tv₁,…,Tvᵣ form a basis of im T: they span by expansion and are independent since a relation puts a combination of vᵢ in ker T. Thus dim V=k+r=dim kerT+dim imT.

tasks.entryDescription: Group action on cosets/subsets; induction using the class equation; polynomial/permutation representation constructions. MIT notes exhibit standard and nonstandard existence proofs.
tasks.currentSketch: For existence, let G act on k-element subsets of itself where |G|=pᵐs and p∤s. The binomial coefficient C(pᵐs,pᵐ) is not divisible by p, so some orbit has size prime to p; its stabilizer has p-part pᵐ and contains a Sylow p-subgroup. For conjugacy, act on cosets G/H; an orbit-count modulo p yields a fixed coset when H is p-subgroup, giving conjugate containment. Conjugation on Sylow subgroups then gives n_p≡1 mod p and n_p||G|.

tasks.routeTitle: Cyclic rotation acts on p-tuples with product 1
tasks.currentSketch: Let C_p cyclically rotate p-tuples (g₁,…,g_p) with product 1. There are |G|^(p−1), divisible by p when p||G|. Nonfixed orbits have size p; fixed tuples are (g,…,g) with g^p=1. The fixed-point count is divisible by p and includes identity, so there is a nonidentity element with g^p=1, hence order p.

tasks.currentSketch: Let G act by conjugation on its p-subgroups; orbit sizes and normalizers constrain subgroup counts. If p divides |G|, a Sylow subgroup exists by Sylow I, so it contains an element of order p by Cauchy's theorem for p-groups (induct via center). This route depends on Sylow existence and is not independent if Sylow is proved using Cauchy.
